correctness.rationale: The log-density derivative yields the unique interior mode for \(d>1\). After the exact substitution \(r=(x/m)^p\), the normalized level equation becomes \(r e^{-r}=e^{-1}y^{p/(d-1)}\). For \(0<y<1\), its negative lies strictly between \(-1/e\) and \(0\), so the two real Lambert-W branches give exactly the lower and upper crossings. Back-substitution proves the full-width and octave formulas. The \(p=1\) specialization reproduces the published ordinary-gamma expression. Numerical spot checks in the packaged script are supplementary and not part of the proof.
